title: Top 16 Buy Now, Pay Later Apps in India For 2026
summary: Learn about the top Indian Buy Now, Pay Later apps for online shopping, bills and more. Compare features, Pros, cons, and more.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Visit most e-commerce checkout pages in India today, and you’ll notice something: buy now pay later options sit right next to UPI and card payments. They are not as widely used, but they are changing the way Indians shop. This shift fascinated us. So we dove down the rabbit hole, testing several pay-later services across different price points.


We’ve compiled this no-nonsense guide to India’s top pay-later apps after comparing user experiences, hidden charges, and acceptance across merchants. But first, here are some nuts-and-bolts…


##


What are Buy Now Pay Later Apps?


[Buy now pay later](https://www.cashfree.com/buy-now-pay-later/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=top-16-buy-now-pay-later-apps-in-india/) apps are digital payment services that let you purchase today while paying for them later.


They give you a short grace period (usually 15-30 days) to settle the bill without interest, or the option to convert larger purchases into monthly installments.


##


What Makes Buy Now Pay Later Apps So Popular?


Who doesn’t love the idea of buying something without paying upfront?


There are multiple reasons these buy now pay later apps are EVERYWHERE now:


- **Getting a credit card in India is still a massive pain** : Many people spend months trying to get one from traditional banks, only to be rejected because of some “technical issues” with documents or no credit history. With pay later apps, users get approved in literal minutes
- **They just feel less serious than a credit card** : Psychologically, it’s easier to think “I’ll pay this small amount later” than to see a credit card bill pile up. (Though those small amounts add up FAST)
- **The convenience is addictive** : Once you’ve experienced the one-click checkout, going back to entering card details feels like torture


Even numbers support this. The buy now pay later market is projected to reach[US$35.07 billion](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/report/india-buy-now-pay-later-market?srsltid=AfmBOoocAYoFfaL3PbU4Pw8IkEqTCpQMUnveN78Jhlyj7qsFfOZ4FJJW) in India by 2030, and it is expected to grow at a CAGR of 9.8% every year.


Plus, most people in smaller cities can’t get credit cards but easily qualify for these services, which explains why they’re blowing up everywhere in India.


Try the[CAGR calculator](https://www.cashfree.com/cagr-calculator/) to get instant insights.


##


How We Chose The Best Buy Now Pay Later Apps


1. The overall user adoption metric
2. User reviews from the Play Store and the App Store
3. Payment success rate and user experience
4. Credit limit ranges and flexibility
5. Merchant ecosystem breadth
6. Customer support responsiveness


##


Our Picks: Top Buy Now Pay Later Apps in India


Now that you know how these buy now pay later apps are picked, let’s get into the specifics.


###


**1. LazyPay**


*Source: LazyPay’s Homepage*


LazyPay is one of India’s leading BNPL platforms. Backed by PayU, it offers payment experiences across 45,000+ online merchants.


It has established itself as a dominant player in the BNPL market as it operates across major e-commerce platforms and food delivery services.


####


**LazyPay best features**


- Offers a credit limit ranging up to ₹1,00,000.
- Personal loans up to ₹5 lakh with instant approval.
- Interest-free period of 15 days with No-cost EMI options for 3, 6, 9, or 12 months.


####


**Pros**


LazyPay has shown strong user growth, particularly in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, per Tech Circle. Customers praise the app’s quick and hassle-free checkout experience that eliminates the need for multiple OTPs during transactions.


####


**Cons**


Reviews on the App Store reveal customer frustration with LazyPay’s collection practices. Additional complaints mention sudden penalties for late payments and technical glitches during the payment process that lead to payment failures.


###


**2. Simpl**


*Source: Simpl’s Homepage*


Simpl functions as a digital “khata” (account) connected to 26,000+ merchants. It offers a one-tap checkout solution that lets users purchase and pay later in bi-monthly cycles.


The company has partnered with quick commerce startup Zepto, extending its one-tap checkout convenience to Zepto Pass members.


####


**Simpl best features**


- Credit limit ranging up to ₹25,000.
- Payment is due on the 3rd of the following month.
- The Pay-In-3 option allows splitting purchases into three installments over 90 days.


####


**Pros**


App Store reviews highlight Simpl’s customer-friendly approach to payment flexibility. Users consistently praise the company’s understanding nature regarding payment extensions.


####


**Cons**


The most frequent complaints about Simpl involve transaction issues and payment processing problems. Play Store reviews describe situations where money is debited from accounts, but transactions remain pending for days.


###


**3. ZestMoney**


*Source: ZestMoney’s Homepage*


ZestMoney is one of the first Buy Now Pay Later platforms in India. It was founded in 2015 to help people make all sorts of purchases without credit cards.


It once reached a valuation of $450 million and raised approximately $140 million from investors, including Goldman Sachs, PayU, and Ribbit Capital. Unfortunately, operations were eventually shut down because of regulatory challenges and business model issues.


####


**ZestMoney best features**


- Its operations ended in late 2023.
- DMI Group acquired the company in early 2024 after its collapse.
- It was a pioneer in paperless EMI options before shutting down.


####


**Pros**


This app gained popularity because it was among the first in the BPNL market to enable first-time online shoppers to purchase through EMIs. This is especially true for electronics, fashion, travel, and education expenses. All in all, purchasers could do all without requiring any debit card or traditional credit score verification.


####


**Cons**


As reported by The Ken, ZestMoney’s high default rates reportedly[reached around 13%](https://the-ken.com/story/why-phonepe-wants-to-buy-zestmoney/?ref=finshots.in) (much higher than the industry standard of 2.5%). The platform also faced operational challenges after regulatory changes by the RBI affected the BNPL sector.


###


**4. Amazon Pay Later**


*Source: Amazon Pay Later’s Homepage*


Amazon Pay Later is a digital credit service that integrates well with the Amazon ecosystem. This 2020-launched service offers instant credit for purchases on Amazon India.


This app is a rebranded version of the Amazon Pay EMI service previously available in the US. The only difference is that this version has additional features tailored for the Indian market.


####


**Amazon Pay Later best features**


- Credit limits vary based on eligibility, with full KYC users accessing higher limits.
- EMI options from 3-12 months with a 1.18% processing fee (including GST).
- Regulatory credit cap of ₹60,000 per year for minimum KYC accounts.


####


**Pros**


As per our research, Amazon Pay Later is for its easy integration with the Amazon shopping experience. Furthermore, buyers love the platform’s simplified dashboard, making it easy to track purchases, repayments, and available credit limits.


####


**Cons**


Amazon Pay Later faces criticism for its restricted usability outside the Amazon ecosystem. Users report inconsistent credit limit increases despite regular on-time payments.


###


**5. Flipkart Pay Later**


*Source: Flipkart Pay Later Website*


Flipkart Pay Later is an integrated payment solution that was introduced in 2017. It integrates well with Myntra and Flipkart.


The service allows users to make purchases with a single click. Furthermore, it consolidates payments into a monthly bill, making the checkout process easy for frequent shoppers.


####


**Flipkart Pay Later best features**


- Credit limit of up to ₹1 lakh with instant approval.
- Pay within 30 days or convert to EMIs.
- EMI tenures range from 3 to 12 months.


####


**Pros**


Flipkart Pay Later offers no-interest credit for payments made before the due date. It also brings simplified single-bill payments for multiple purchases.


####


**Cons**


Customer reviews on Google Play Store and App Store tell us that the app is limited primarily to the Flipkart ecosystem. This restricts its utility compared to more versatile BNPL options. Some reviews also report unexpected changes to credit limits and payment terms with no notice.


###


**6. Paytm Postpaid**


*Source: Paytm Postpaid’s Homepage*


Paytm Postpaid is integrated with[India’s popular UPI platform](https://blogrevamp.cashfree.com/top-upi-apps-in-india/) , Paytm. This app helps users shop and cover everyday expenses like bill payments, fuel purchases, and groceries. In other words, it simplifies routine financial transactions.


The service operates on a monthly billing cycle with 7 days to repay; if you avail of their service on 1st April 2025, you must repay the amount on or before the due date, i.e., 7th May 2025.


####


**PayTM Postpaid best features**


- You get a credit limit up to ₹60,000 with 0% interest upto 30 days.
- It is usable for both online and offline merchant payments.
- It is easy to integrate with Paytm’s broader financial ecosystem.


####


**Pros**


The platform has a wide merchant acceptance network that allows users to use their credit lines at select physical and online stores.


####


**Cons**


Customer complaints highlight challenges in seeking assistance via the customer support team when needed. Moreover, some users also report unexpected credit limit reductions and account restrictions without a clear explanation.


###


**7. Freecharge Pay Later**


*Source: Freecharge Pay Later’s Homepage*


So Freecharge Pay Later was this cool BNPL option backed by Axis Bank that gave you about 10,000 in credit each month. They shut it down last December.


If you go to their website now, you’ll just see a message saying the service isn’t available anymore. Kind of a bummer if you were using it regularly.


####


**Freecharge Pay Later best features**


- Offered a 10,000 monthly limit with a 30-day credit window.
- Featured secured single-tap technology.
- Seamless integration with the Freecharge wallet enables you to make payments easily.


####


**Pros**


The whole setup was pretty easy; you could shop whenever you wanted and pay the bill once a month on the 5th. There was no need to juggle multiple due dates, which was a huge relief for most users.


####


**Cons**


The biggest headache? They’d generate your bill and make it due on the same day, giving people zero breathing room to pay for the thing. Another thing that bugged users was finding out it showed up on their credit report as a personal loan from Axis Bank. Miss a payment, and boom—your credit score takes a hit.


###


**8. OlaMoney Postpaid**


*Source: OlaMoney Postpaid’s Homepage*


Ola is a popular brand in the transportation sector. To avoid the hassle of paying every time you ride with them, they introduced the OlaMoney Postpaid service.


This service started as a way to pay for your Ola rides at the end of every month. However, later, they expanded it to cover pretty much everything—bills, food, shopping, you name it.


It’s not for everyone, though. They only invite certain Ola users based on how often they use the service.


####


**Ola Money best features**


- Credit limit of up to ₹5,000 with exact limits personalized to each user and viewable in the Ola app.
- Flexible billing cycle of 15 to 30 days based on individual user profiles.
- Service extends beyond ride payments to cover utility bills, DTH recharge, mobile recharge, food, shopping, and various online services.


####


**Pros**


The best part about OlaMoney Postpaid has to be how convenient it makes booking multiple Ola rides. You don’t have to mess around with payments every single time – just hop in, hop out, and deal with everything later in one go.


####


**Cons**


Good luck figuring out how to get an invite if you don’t have one already. Plus, it’s way less useful outside the Ola universe – doesn’t work nearly as many places as something like Amazon Pay Later or Simpl.


###


**9. Mobikwik Zip**


*Source: Mobikwik Zip’s Homepage*


MobiKwik ZIP is MobiKwik’s extension of its wallet services into the credit space. It has created what it describes as a “digital credit card” with limits up to ₹60,000 that integrates directly with your digital wallet.


The concept ensures users always have a financial safety net available whenever needed.


####


**Mobikwik Zip best features**


- ZIP EMI offers funds/loans up to ₹5, 00,000 as per the official app.
- One-time, non-refundable activation fee ranging between ₹99 to ₹399 inclusive of applicable taxes.
- Enables users to shop across more than 1 lakh brands, per Bank Bazaar.


####


**Pros**


Great for time-sensitive situations, such as when utility bills are due before your salary arrives. Users appreciate how it integrates seamlessly with the familiar MobiKwik wallet interface, eliminating any learning curve.


####


**Cons**


Customer service is an area where MobiKwik ZIP could improve. Some users have reported delayed responses when account issues arise, which can be frustrating when trying to resolve time-sensitive matters.


###


**10. Tata Neu Credit (NeuPass)**


*Source: Tata Neu’s Homepage*


Tata Neu’s credit offering is part of its comprehensive super-app strategy centered around the Tata brand ecosystem. It’s connected to its NeuPass membership program, which offers enhanced benefits when shopping with any Tata brand.


Rather than functioning as a standalone BNPL service, it’s integrated as a feature within the broader Tata Neu platform.


####


**Tata Neu best features**


- Integrates with numerous Tata brands, including Air India, Croma, BigBasket, IHCL hotels, Tata Cliq, Westside, and Tata 1mg.
- NeuPass membership provides a minimum of 5% additional NeuCoins on app purchases.
- Each NeuCoin has a value of ₹1 with no limits on earning or redemptions.


####


**Pros**


Regular shoppers at Tata properties like BigBasket, Westside, or Croma can earn up to 7% back in NeuCoins. This represents a competitive rewards rate compared to many credit card programs.


####


**Cons**


The service has limited utility for those who don’t regularly shop within the Tata ecosystem. Some financial forum discussions suggest that traditional credit cards may offer more flexibility than ecosystem-specific BNPL services.


###


**11. Kissht**


*Source: Kissht’s Homepage*


Kissht is an inclusive credit platform made to serve people who might find traditional banking criteria challenging.


Founded as a digital lending solution for instant financing needs, the company has steadily expanded its presence throughout India. Their focus centers particularly on EMI-based credit for retail transactions.


####


**Kissht best features**


- Offers personal loans reaching ₹5 lakhs.
- Shopping options expand with access to 3,000+ physical and 50+ online stores.
- Their Digital EMI card transforms approval into immediate purchasing power.


####


**Pros**


Kissht has simplified the loan process in a way that makes credit more accessible. The platform receives particular appreciation for its straightforward approach that doesn’t require deep financial literacy or familiarity with complex banking terminology.


####


**Cons**


Some reviews mention concerns about payment collection practices. Several customers have also noted occasional delays between loan approval and fund disbursement. This can affect time-sensitive financial planning.


###


**12. Capital Float (now axio)**


*Source: Capital Float’s Homepage*


Capital Float decided to rebrand in 2022 and started calling itself “axio.” This Bangalore-based company provides a comprehensive suite of consumer products to small and medium enterprises.


Capital Float provides buy now, pay later services at checkout of various e-commerce platforms like Amazon, MakeMyTrip, and Razorpay. Additionally, they help you manage your expenses with their integration with Walnut, a money management app.


####


**Axio best features**


- Works with big names like Amazon, making checkout super easy.
- EMI options from 3 to 12 months.
- Found extra money to repay early? You won’t face any prepayment penalties.


####


**Pros**


As per 5paisa, about two-thirds of their new customers are from outside the top ten cities in India. This is huge considering how most fintech companies ignore small-town India.


####


**Cons**


According to many app reviews, customer service is a nightmare. One frustrated user called their agents “harassing goons” in their App Store review. The app also misses some basic expense tracking features.


###


**13. ePayLater**


*Source: ePay Later’s Homepage*


ePayLater is the BNPL platform that cares about small businesses, not just shoppers. These folks focus on providing instant credit to kirana stores and small retail businesses that form the backbone of India’s retail economy.


It’s solving a real problem since most small shops operate on thin margins and need credit to stock up.


####


**ePayLater best features**


- Credit limits extend to ₹25 lakhs for businesses looking to manage inventory.
- Take advantage of 14 to 30 days of interest-free to align with your cash flow cycle.
- No processing fees, hidden charges, or unexpected costs.


####


**Pros**


Small business owners swear by ePayLater for managing their cash flow problems. The credit period of 14 to 30 days gives them breathing room to stock up inventory at competitive prices and pay when they’ve made sales, rather than upfront.


####


**Cons**


Some merchants complain that the approval process seems random; two identical businesses might get different credit limits for no reason. Customer service is criticized in reviews for being super slow to respond when payment issues arise.


###


**14. FlexPay by Vivifi**


*Source: FlexPay’s Homepage*


FlexPay by Vivifi is doing something genuinely innovative that most other BNPL players haven’t figured out – bringing credit to payments.


They launched a “Scan Now and Pay Later” feature that lets you use credit at any UPI merchant. This is basically everywhere in India these days. It’s targeting the massive chunk of Indians who don’t have or can’t get credit cards.


####


**FlexPay best features**


- UPI-based credit that works at millions of UPI-accepting merchants across India.
- Credit limits up to ₹3 lakhs for eligible customers with a minimum monthly income of ₹8,000.
- Super flexible repayment options without rigid EMI structures.


####


**Pros**


Unlike other BNPL options that force you into specific repayment schedules, FlexPay lets you pay back however much you want, whenever you want.


####


**Cons**


Users mention that the interest can rack up quickly if you stretch out repayments too long. A common complaint is that the app tends to glitch during peak hours, which is precisely when you don’t want payment failures to happen.


###


**15. Freo Pay**


*Source: Freo Pay’s Homepage*


Freo Pay is a Bangalore-based BNPL platform founded in 2021. Freo Pay is all about keeping things super simple. They offer instant credit up to ₹15,000 with zero interest for 30 days.


You can use it anywhere in India by scanning QR codes. It’s clearly at younger users who need small credit lines for everyday expenses.


Apart from this, middle-aged people could also use Freo Pay. They could avail of their personal loan facility that has an offer range of 3000 INR- 3 lakh INR. This service comes with flexible repayment terms (2-36 months).


####


**Freo Pay best features**


- Zero interest credit for a full 30 days.
- Works through UPI so you can pay at any[QR code](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-qr-code/) in India.
- Super quick 5-minute approval with minimal documentation.


####


**Pros**


The app scores major points for its clean, straightforward design. It doesn’t have the million confusing features that banking apps usually offer. You can literally just scan, pay, and worry about it next month.


####


**Cons**


The credit limit is pretty tiny compared to other options – maxing out at just ₹10,000 initially, which doesn’t get you far these days. And if you miss your payment deadline? Expect to be hit with a daily late fee of ₹30 that can add up to ₹900 plus GST, which is steep for such small credit amounts.


###


**16. Slice**


*Source: Slice’s Homepage*


Slice started as a challenger to credit cards. It specifically targets young people and students who couldn’t qualify for traditional cards.


Slice has changed over time and now offers a mix of banking and credit products with credit limits ranging up to Rupees 30 lakhs per year. It’s positioned as the accessible and youth-friendly option in the market.


####


**Slice best features**


- Daily credit limit of 3 lakh for financial flexibility.
- Enjoy an annual ceiling of 30 lakhs for comprehensive financial planning.
- Convert bills into EMIs with minimum interest charges.


####


**Pros**


The app is clean, modern, and intuitive: unlike traditional bank apps that seem designed by people who hate smartphones. Another big plus is transparency; they explain fees clearly without hiding them in 20 pages of legal jargon that nobody reads.


####


**Cons**


The app gets mixed reviews for customer service. While some folks have great experiences, some complain about getting robotic responses to genuine problems.


##


Buy Now Pay Later Apps Have Changed The Way India Pays


The[buy now pay later](https://www.cashfree.com/buy-now-pay-later/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=top-16-buy-now-pay-later-apps-in-india/) scene in India is exciting, a bit chaotic, and changing by the minute. But these services make spending easier, which isn’t always a good thing.


If you can’t afford it in two paychecks, maybe the fancy new gadget can wait. Remember when mom would say, “money doesn’t grow on trees”? Turns out she was onto something.


The bottom line is that these apps are tools, not magic money machines. Use them like you would a sharp knife: carefully and with respect for what they can do.
